implementation_status: Original H.264 controls, independent fixtures and isolated decoder resource/FIFO diagnostics implemented; input DMA not qualified, frame decode and encode not implemented

target.encoder_api: V4L2; select an upstream interface after the hardware control model is established
target.userspace: GStreamer v4l2codecs for Request API decoding
target.codec_firmware: no proprietary codec firmware or libvcodec dependency in the target implementation

provenance.implementation_inputs: Published hardware interface facts, public GPL MediaTek kernel register definitions, public Linux UAPI and independently observed hardware behavior
provenance.note: Existing kernel framework and resource drivers are open source. This is an independent implementation target, not a claim that a formally separated clean-room project has already been completed.

sources.scope: Public encoder UAPI; software bitstream construction in kernel discouraged
Userspace integration target; not yet qualified on Gemini
Open GPL MT6797 VDEC power sequence at 0x300, SRAM PDN bit 8 and ACK bit 12; matches current framework. Read-only snapshot 0xe0d is not evidence that bits 9-11 must be changed.
Public GPL resource/clock/IRQ/mmap glue only; codec mapping uses pgprot_noncached
Public architecture definition: pgprot_noncached uses Device-nGnRnE

coverage.functional_specification: Sections 6.7 and 6.8 describe CPU-programmed decoding/encoding. No conclusion about a mandatory codec firmware follows from the upstream VPU/SCP driver.
coverage.decoder_register_table: Section 4.7, pages 799-820, documents VDEC_GCON, not the frame-programming banks.
coverage.encoder_register_table: Section 4.8, pages 821-822, documents three clock/chip-enable registers, not frame programming.
coverage.existing_kernel: Accepted kernel has no MT6797 mtk-vcodec match and omits the VDECSYS provider. Isolated e87e65549920 candidate enables the existing open-source provider, larb1 and a direct decoder DT node. No hardware video driver is installed as the accepted default; existing video nodes are JPEG only.
coverage.related_silicon: Public MT8173 kernel hardware verification code supplies candidate H.264 frame/slice, scaling SRAM, reference, bitstream and reset interfaces. Their compatibility with MT6797 remains subject to hardware tests.

missing_contracts: MT6797 qualification of candidate decoder frame/slice register fields and sequencing, including references, quantization and start/completion
Encoder source/reference/bitstream buffer fields, picture commands, rate control and completion
Exact decoded tile layout, strides and alignment, including mapping to a Linux pixel format
Scratch-buffer sizes and lifetimes, DMA alignment and address units
MT6797 qualification of decoder interrupt status and acknowledge sequence (SPI 240 level-low resource is known)
Reset/timeout recovery that quiesces DMA before returning or freeing buffers

required: Decoded output compared against software reference across intra, inter, multi-slice and resolution-change cases
Encoded output decoded by an independent software decoder and checked against quality/rate targets
Malformed controls, invalid references, timeout, streamoff, close, suspend and repeated-open tests
On-board measurement of throughput, CPU use, thermals and IOMMU/kernel errors

host_tests.coverage: Independent SPS/PPS and slice word fixtures, signed QP, bounds and atomic rejection, 4x4/8x8 Linux scaling-list order, SRAM locations and coefficient byte order

register_probe_result.note: SMI and all decoder clock votes are present, but expected AVC readback was not obtained. Later FIFO probes found both local power-down masks initially 0xffffffff. The early probe does not initialize those masks. Zero readback neither proves incompatibility nor validates programming; no frame was submitted.
register_probe_result.clock_rate_source: clk_get_rate; configured rate, not an independently measured frequency

resource_candidate.clock_rate_source: clk_get_rate; supplier snapshots are control/status reads, not frequency measurements

fifo_probe.status: All seventeen input fetches timed out; no known barrel bytes obtained

attempts.reason: Initial read-only SSH health guard timed out before upload or module load

fifo_probe.note: Boot qualification is separate from input/frame proof. Trials 01-04 retained mappings until reboot. Trial 05, both trial-07 matrices and trial 08 acknowledged documented break/idle and unloaded normally. Trial 06 did not load a module because its initial SSH health guard timed out. No frame DMA was started.
fifo_probe.current_stop_contract: MT6797 documented MISC break command, both acknowledgement bits, then idle reset; uncertain stop pins mappings, power and module until reboot
fifo_probe.current_global_clock_control: Documented VDEC_GCON 0x18 bit 0 disables global automatic clock-off; programmed through existing syscon regmap, clock and reset registers left to frameworks
fifo_probe.observed_stop: Trial 05: both break acknowledgement bits 0x11 and idle reset passed; mappings, clocks and power released and the module unloaded normally despite failed input comparison.
fifo_probe.current_write_ordering: Each APB write completes with arm64 mb() / DSB SY, matching the public sync_write primitive; per-attempt sources distinguish versions.
fifo_probe.endpoint_note: Early DMA30 allocation could place the exclusive FIFO end at 1 GiB. Current code allocates a trailing guard and rejects an endpoint beyond the DMA mask; the padded trial-07 matrix still timed out with both endpoint words fitting 24 bits.
fifo_probe.current_mapping: Codec banks use resource-managed non-posted Device-nGnRnE by default, matching the public MT6797 driver userspace mapping; trial 08 still timed out

supplier_snapshot.interpretation: VDEC power acknowledgements set; reset released, isolation/clock-disable/SRAM-PDN bit8 and SRAM-ACK bit12 clear. PLL control 0x121, PCW 0xd0000, power 0x80000001 and mux 0x81010100 observed. Configured 338 MHz, not independently measured. Bits9-11 remain set; the matching public MT6797 power implementation uses only SRAM bit8, so the snapshot does not justify additional power writes.

related_silicon_reference.compatibility_evidence: All seven H.264 register-bank bases match the MT6797 functional specification. CONFIG_CHIP_VER_CURR=80 selects the MT8580-class VLD_TOP path in this MT8173 kernel test interface. Bank matching is not proof of command, tile-layout or DMA compatibility.

implemented_components.control_translator: research/mt6797-vdec/mt6797-h264-controls.c; progressive 8-bit 4:2:0 SPS/PPS, slice-header fields, scaling-SRAM packing, signed fields and atomic validation
implemented_components.register_probe: research/mt6797-vdec/probe.c; separate temporary module, no DMA buffers, IRQ registration or frame start
implemented_components.fifo_probe: research/mt6797-vdec/fifo-probe.c; proper DT/IOMMU device, bounded private input-fetch comparison, no frame start; unproven DMA kept mapped and powered until supervised reboot
implemented_components.fixture_generator: research/mt6797-vdec/make-pcm-fixture.py; original baseline I_PCM syntax and pixel gradients, every sample independently decoded by FFmpeg
implemented_components.frame_comparator: research/mt6797-vdec/compare-frame.py; explicit NV12/MM21 unpacking and full reference comparison, software layout tests only
implemented_components.supplier_probe: research/mt6797-vdec/supplier-probe.c; read-only snapshot of existing scpsys power, PLL and mux control/status registers while a separate resource vote is held; no frequency measurement
